parsed.explanation: The operative regime combines an on-the-books gender-presentation offence (Section 379, up to 3 months) reaching any visibly trans visitor in public, a 10–14-year same-sex conduct statute, zero protective legislation, and — critically — documented state security-force harassment, arrest, detention, torture and beating of LGBTQI+ people across 2018–2022, plus a 2017 ministerial call to arrest and detain LGBTQ persons. Enforcement of the conduct statute is undocumented for five years, but state targeting is not hypothetical: torture in custody is a severity-5 feature, civic infrastructure was destroyed by force, and most openly LGBTQI+ citizens fled. The dress offence is a traveller-facing universal exposure with no remedy. Thin-data extrapolation from criminalisation, hostile official rhetoric, absent recourse and documented custodial violence resolves well below any 0.65 anchor; custodial torture and state-directed threat-framing place this in the upper High Risk band, just above the 0.25 extortion/raid anchors because the documented state hand and violence are worse.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented: no data on visa or marker screening of trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: No entry-stage exposure documented, but absence of documentation is not safety in a state whose forces target LGBTQI+ persons once identified.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: security forces harassed, arrested, detained, tortured and beat LGBTQI+ persons 2018–2022; 2017 ministerial statement ordering arrest and detention of LGBTQ persons; community-group staff detained months without charge. Custodial violence is the operative detention reality.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None; no hate-crime law, no recourse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any outing to police can flow directly into abusive custody with no remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Section 379 criminalises male presentation as female nationwide — a universal public-presentation exposure for trans visitors; no facility data otherwise.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Presentation itself is a police lever independent of any conduct allegation.

care_services.exposure: Not documented: no data on gender-affirming care access or HRT import for visitors.
care_services.interaction: Undocumented; thin-data extrapolation gives no credit where criminalisation and hostility dominate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: head-of-state rhetoric that homosexuality is alien and will never be supported; 2017 ministerial call for arrests and detention until procreation; nationwide criminalisation of conduct and dress.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Only sectoral harassment protection for oil-and-gas employees (2020) — no general recourse.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses the documented custodial abuse; NGOs blocked by NGO Act.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented: no age-specific rules; a minor travelling with a parent faces the same dress law and social stigma; no formal exposure attaching to the minor is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family visibility could raise outing risk; not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: widespread societal discrimination and stigmatisation; police are the abusers rather than protectors; most openly LGBTQI+ citizens have fled.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None; no hate-crime statute; reporting to police plausibly worsens outcome.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims have effectively no recourse; visitors are isolated soft targets.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No enforcement record of the conduct provision 2018–2022 is genuine but thin; whether the 2017 order was formalised is unknown; no prosecutions under Section 379 documented either way.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns resolve toward the risk structural facts imply: criminalisation, hostile state, no relief, no community infrastructure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's regime is systematic but non-lethal (exclusion, humiliation, fines). This dossier documents torture and beatings by state security forces against LGBTQI+ people, a destroyed civic sector, and official calls for detention — materially worse than 0.35-A.

Similar tier: on-the-books presentation offence, birth-sex-type state harshness, documented custodial abuse. This jurisdiction adds torture, an explicit ministerial arrest directive, and complete absence of any protection or community — sits at or slightly above 0.25-C.

0.55-B features administrative screening friction with working appeal desks and no violence. Here remedies are absent, police are perpetrators, and torture is documented — this regime is clearly below 0.55-B.

0.15-A shows routine arrests of mismatched travellers with months of beaten pretrial custody and illusory appeals. The dress statute here is unenforced on record, and conduct enforcement is absent for five years, keeping this above 0.15 — but the documented torture and flight of the openly LGBTQI+ population are close in kind.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a single national criminalising layer with no protective counterweight: a presentation offence that reaches every visibly trans visitor in public, a severe conduct statute, and a documented pattern of state security forces abusing, detaining and torturing LGBTQI+ people between 2018 and 2022 despite non-enforcement of the conduct provision. Official rhetoric and a ministerial directive to arrest LGBTQ persons constitute state threat-framing (tier 2, approaching tier 1 in custody). No remedy operates: no hate-crime law, no functioning community, citizens fleeing. The severity of what follows outing — custodial torture with impunity — dominates the modest probability discount from non-enforcement records, resolving just above the 0.25 anchors and well below the 0.35 systematic-but-non-lethal regime.
